title: DaVinci Resolve 21.1 Release: Integrates Claude Code and ChatGPT Codex

content_html:
The ultimate efficiency tool for editors is here. Blackmagic Design officially released the video editing software DaVinci Resolve 21.1 on September 8th. This update brings a breakthrough in intelligent upgrades, fully integrating a group of top AI assistants such as Claude, Claude Code, and ChatGPT Codex.

In terms of core features, users can now interact with AI using everyday language, allowing it to handle previously tedious routine tasks. Whether analyzing projects in a large media library, intelligently organizing media files, adjusting software settings, or performing batch video rendering, AI can easily manage these tasks. Moreover, editors just need to give instructions to the AI assistant, which can precisely edit highlight clips from long videos, automatically remove redundant footage, and even directly assist in rendering the final video. This transformation will completely free creators from inefficient and repetitive labor, allowing them to spend more time and energy on pure creative concepts.

Aside from the highly anticipated AI assistant matrix, the new version has also made several practical improvements in traditional imaging hardware and workflow compatibility. The DaVinci photo page has been significantly expanded and now natively supports popular camera models such as Fujifilm GFX and X series, Leica SL, and Sony α7R VI. Photographers and editors can directly import raw format photos from these cameras for processing after daily shooting, eliminating the cumbersome format conversion process and achieving efficient output with seamless integration.

In addition, DaVinci Resolve 21.1 further optimizes and upgrades the multi-camera workflow based on actual post-production pain points, greatly improving the smoothness of multi-angle switching and synchronization. At the same time, the software has introduced new graphic tools in this update, providing creators with more rich and detailed expression methods for visual effects, color grading, and image editing.
